title: Comparison Inside the ALU: SLT, the Sign Bit and the Overflow Correction
unit: Design of the Arithmetic and Logic Unit
quickIdea: An ALU compares by subtracting and looking at the result. The sign bit of A - B says whether A < B, but only when the subtraction did not overflow - so the honest signal is sign XOR overflow.
remember: Comparison is not a separate arithmetic: it is subtraction plus a look at the result's sign or at the carry out.
For signed operands, the sign bit of A - B gives A < B only if no overflow occurred; the standard fix is Less = sign(A - B) XOR overflow.
For unsigned operands, the carry out of A - B tells you the answer instead: carry 1 means no borrow, so A >= B.
A real ALU exposes a single Less line to bit 0 only: the top slice computes it, and every other slice is told zero.
A direct comparator built from a recursive greater-than definition exists, but most designs reuse the subtractor because it is already there.

example.prompt: In 4-bit two's complement, compute A < B for A = -8 and B = 1 by subtracting, and explain what goes wrong with the plain sign bit.
example.work: -8 - 1 = -9, which is below the 4-bit range -8 to 7. The subtraction is 1000 + 1110 + 1 = 1 0111, and keeping 0111 gives +7 with carry out 1. The sign bit is now 0, which would claim -8 < 1 is false. The carries into and out of the sign column differ, so overflow is 1; sign XOR overflow is 0 XOR 1 = 1, correctly saying A < B.
example.answer: The sign bit alone says false; sign XOR overflow says true, which is correct.

gateAngle: Comparison questions rarely ask for the comparison itself; they ask which flag a branch reads, or whether a given ALU can produce a comparison at all. GATE CSE 2003 Q.46 is the negative case: with only K and C0, the circuit cannot produce A+1, and the same reasoning tells you whether it could produce a comparison - only if a Less signal is exposed.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: A 4-bit ALU produces only sign and overflow. For which of these pairs is sign XOR overflow the right answer to A < B: (5, 3), (-8, 1), (3, 5)?
variations.answer: All three, and it is right for all three; the point is that it is right for (-8, 1) where the plain sign bit fails.
variations.why: The corrected signal agrees with the sign bit whenever no overflow occurs, and fixes exactly the overflow cases.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: Why does the ALU need a separate unsigned comparison path rather than reusing Less?
variations.answer: Because Less is built from the sign bit, which only means anything for signed values; for unsigned values the carry out is the meaningful signal.
variations.why: This is the same split as the two overflow flags: one bit cannot answer both questions.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: How many gate delays does an equality comparison add on top of a subtraction, and how many does a less-than add?
variations.answer: Equality adds the zero-detect tree over the result bits; less-than adds nothing beyond the sign and overflow bits already produced.
variations.why: This is why a branch-on-equal costs the same ALU cycle as a subtract, while the comparison result for less-than is available as a by-product.

trap.what: Using the sign bit of A - B as the answer to A < B.
trap.why: When the subtraction overflows, the truncated result has the wrong sign, so the comparison flips.
trap.counterexample: 4-bit: A = -8, B = 1. A - B = -9 wraps to +7 with sign 0, yet A really is less than B. Only sign XOR overflow recovers the truth.

check.question: In 4-bit two's complement, take A = 7 and B = -8. What are the sign bit and the overflow bit of A - B, and is A < B?
check.answer: Sign 1, overflow 1, sign XOR overflow = 0, so A < B is reported false, which is correct because 7 > -8.
check.explanation: 7 - (-8) = 15, which is outside -8 to 7, so the kept result is 1111 = -1: the sign bit is 1 and the carries into and out of the sign column differ, so overflow is 1. The XOR cancels the misleading sign and gives the true answer. Always recompute the carries rather than guessing the flag.

sourceLine: Comparison by subtraction, the Less signal routed from the top slice to bit 0, and the note that the top slice detects both sign and overflow: Curt Nelson's chapter 3 slides (English, read in part). The two ways of comparing - subtract and test, or build a direct comparator from a recursive greater-than - and the warning that the sign is meaningful only for signed numbers: Anshul Kumar, Lecture 12 (English, read in part). The overflow correction is recomputed by enumeration over all 4-bit pairs in scripts/validate.py.
